# R118 quant section (generated by quant.py)

Descriptive only; signal source: none. The index's 1-minute closes (unfilled) and the options' own prints.

## L1. Variance risk premium: the variance the straddle priced against the variance that came

implied = (straddle / (0.798 x spot))^2, the variance of the index's log move to the close that the ATM straddle prices; realised = the sum of squared 1-minute log returns over the same minutes. Ratio > 1: options priced more movement than came.

Caution: on expiry days the index mean-reverts minute to minute (L3: VR(30) about 0.76), so the sum of 1-minute squared returns overstates the variance that matters for a move to the close, most for SENSEX and MIDCPNIFTY. L2's close-move test has no such bias; read the by-index premium there.

## L2. The close's move against a normal (bell-curve) move of the size the straddle priced

z = log(close / spot at t) / implied sd. If the straddle priced a normal move correctly, |z| would follow a standard normal: P(|move| > 1 straddle) = P(|z| > 0.798) = 42.5%, P(> 2 straddles) = 11.0%, P(> 3) = 1.7%.

sd of z below 1: the 12:00 straddle priced more than the typical move to the close (the premium is rich); above 1: cheap. H1 / H2 under 30 days are small samples.

Reading: fewer small-to-medium moves than a bell curve, and about as many (or more) big ones: the classic fat-tailed shape. The straddle is dear for the typical day and roughly fair or cheap for the rare big one.

## L4. The market's probability against what happened (OTM options priced Rs 0.50+, every mark)

p_itm = N(d2) from the option's own Black-76 IV (forward = spot, r = 0, calendar time to 15:30): the risk-neutral chance it ends in the money. 'ended ITM' uses the index's last minute (a proxy for the exchange's settlement price). 'payout / price' = mean end value / mean price: 1.00 means buyers got back, on average, exactly what they paid (before any costs); 95% range from 1,000 day-bootstraps.
